key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This approach can accelerate interface screening, while modification with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces buried-interface damage and improves UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe degradation at different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements during UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized preferential UV degradation to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved stability with silane modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or validation that UV-soaking results predict long-term performance under full operating conditions.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
